heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 handles Overture PETG flawlessly out of the box using its standard direct-drive toolhead and stock stainless steel nozzle without needing an enclosure. Adhering to the 14 mm³/s volumetric flow limit maintains an optimal safe printing speed of 167 mm/s while preventing under-extrusion and stringing.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin layer of glue stick or liquid glue as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in the filament profile to cap travel speeds automatically at 167 mm/s.
Enable 'Wipe while Retracting' with a 2 mm wipe distance to minimize nozzle tip buildup and fine wisps.
Turn off the auxiliary part cooling fan completely (0%) to eliminate draft-induced warping and premature layer chilling.
Set Pressure Advance (Flow Dynamics) to 0.040 to prevent corner bulging and oozing across travel moves.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Excessive wispy stringing and nozzle blob accumulation
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Material has absorbed ambient moisture or retraction wipe settings are disabled.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dehydrate the spool in a filament dryer at 65°C for 6 hours, enable 2 mm retraction wipe, and reduce nozzle temp to 235°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer tearing or permanently bonding to build sheet
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG creates an overly aggressive chemical bond with bare PEI surfaces when printed hot.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVP glue stick or Bambu Liquid Glue onto the Textured PEI Plate to serve as a sacrificial release layer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Brittle layer adhesion and perimeter separation
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive cooling fan airflow quenching extruded plastic before molecular bonding occurs.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Clamp part cooling between 20% minimum and 50% maximum, and increase nozzle temperature to 245°C.

faq.question: Do I need an enclosure to print Overture PETG on the Bambu Lab A1?
faq.answer: No, PETG prints optimally in an open-frame environment; excessive ambient chamber heat can induce heat creep and filament softening in the extruder.

faq.question: Can the stock Bambu A1 stainless steel nozzle handle this filament?
faq.answer: Yes, standard Overture PETG is non-abrasive, meaning the stock stainless steel nozzle will not experience premature wear.

faq.question: Why is the filament popping and leaving rough surface voids?
faq.answer: PETG is highly hygroscopic; steam bubbles formed during extrusion cause popping and voids, requiring 6-8 hours of drying at 65°C.

faq.question: Why is the top surface finish cloudy or uneven at high speeds?
faq.answer: Exceeding the melt capacity causes uneven crystallization; ensure volumetric flow is strictly capped at 14 mm³/s and slow top surface speed to 100 mm/s.
